changelog: First public release of fx-stash — premium personal & shared stash system (QBCore / Qbox / ESX).

Fixed: a job-restricted stash could reject every player with that job. Two separate causes stacked on top of each other. First, the rule inputs in the admin panel only wrote their value to the draft on blur — typing a job name and pressing Save without clicking elsewhere sent an empty name, and the server silently drops rules with a blank name, so the stash ended up with zero rules and nobody matched. Second, even a correctly saved rule was matched case-sensitively against the framework's job name, so a rule saved as "Police" never matched qb-core's "police". Both are fixed: every rule input now writes on every keystroke, and job/gang matching is case-insensitive on the server. Turning on Config.Debug now also logs the exact job, grade and rule count involved when access is denied, so a mismatch is visible in the console instead of a bare "no access" notification.
Fixed: qb-core builds where job.grade or gang.grade is a plain number instead of a {level=...} table crashed the access check instead of reading the grade. Both shapes are now accepted.

Fixed: a stash created while the owner was inside a routing bucket (an instance) could not be opened by anyone, including its creator. The admin panel always reported bucket 0 for the current position, so the stash was saved with bucket 0, and the server-side proximity check compares the player's real bucket against the stash's stored bucket. The bucket is no longer taken from the client at all — the server stamps the creator's actual routing bucket when the stash is created.

New admin panel: a tablet-style shell replaces the old flat panel, and creating or editing a stash is now a 5-step wizard (Basics, Capacity, Access, Location, Summary) with per-step validation instead of one long form. Each access type shows what it does before you fill in rules, and the final step shows every setting for one last check before saving.

Fixed: the edit screen had no way to change a stash's coordinates at all — the field simply did not exist, so "move this stash" meant delete and recreate it. The new Location step has a coordinate card with the current X/Y/Z/heading and three ways to set it: your current position, manual entry, or the new laser picker.

New: a laser coordinate picker — aim at any point in the world (ground or object) and a crosshair HUD shows the live X/Y/Z and distance to it, confirm with E or cancel with Backspace. This sits alongside the existing prop/ped drag-placement flow and does not replace it.

FiveM's NUI does not support the CSS backdrop-filter property, so every panel, modal, toast and HUD badge that relied on it for its blurred-glass look rendered as a flat, un-blurred tint instead (or, if the tint was removed, as a floating shape with no glass effect at all). All backdrop-filter usage is removed and replaced with the game's own native screen blur (TriggerScreenblurFadeIn/Out), guarded the same way fx-admin's panel is: a running fade is cancelled before the opposite one starts, so rapidly opening and closing the panel cannot leave the blur stuck on screen. Blur turns on when the panel opens and off during prop/ped placement, the laser picker and the object picker, so the world stays clear while you are looking at it.

Removed the full-page dark scrim behind the panel and behind every modal (the stash wizard, import, confirm and object-picker dialogs) — with the panel already blurring the game behind it, the extra tint read as a black curtain covering the whole screen. Depth now comes from the game blur alone; panel and cards keep their own border and shadow.

Fixed several inputs in the wizard (job/gang/identifier rule fields, the custom model field, the ped scenario field) rendering as an unstyled white browser default box instead of the themed input — they were missing a type attribute, and the CSS only matched input[type=text] explicitly. The selector now covers any input regardless of type, so a missing type attribute can no longer slip through unstyled again.

Fixed the rule-row delete button not lining up with its input fields, and the identifier rule row giving most of its width to the type dropdown instead of the value field. Added a visible focus ring on inputs, and gave every theme's input field its own background distinct from button/chip surfaces — inputs previously used the same surface color as buttons and were only visible by their border.

Fixed the scrollbar thumb being nearly invisible in the Light theme (and low-contrast in the others) — it used the same faint color as borders. The thumb now uses each theme's muted-text color, which stays readable against both light and dark surfaces, with a hover and active state.

Security: all data coming from the client is now validated on the server before use, through a new central guard module. Stash name, weight, slots, category, access rules, coordinates and world data are type-checked, range-clamped and whitelisted rather than written to the database as-is; money deposit/withdraw amounts and target server IDs are rejected outright (not clamped) when out of range, so a negative or absurd amount can no longer be silently coerced into a valid one. Opening a stash and depositing/withdrawing money now re-checks the player's actual server-side distance to the stash instead of trusting the client's claim of being nearby. Every player-facing net event and callback is rate-limited. Every call into another resource's export is wrapped so a missing or broken target inventory/target system cannot crash fx-stash.

Cleanup: removed a leftover frameworks.lua at the resource root from an unrelated RedM project (VORP/RSG references, never loaded by this resource's manifest) and the internal development spec setup.md. Added a proper setup/ folder (SQL install script, ace-permission snippet, custom-inventory integration guide) and marked config.lua, config_server.lua, framework/*.lua and locales/*.json as escrow_ignore so they stay editable after purchase.

All server-facing exports that return a stash object now return a copy, not a live reference into the internal cache, so another resource can no longer mutate fx-stash's state by editing the object it got back.
